title: Unify telemetry enrichment and attach runbook sections to incident channels
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When incidents fire from the observability stack, on-call engineers spend 5-20 minutes collecting the relevant telemetry (trace spans, last 5 minutes of logs, top error groups, and the related Grafana panels) and the runbook sections that are relevant to the service/component. This slows time-to-detect and time-to-recover and leads to duplicated manual work in Slack/PagerDuty channels.

Goal: Build an automated enrichment pipeline that attaches a concise telemetry snapshot and the most-relevant runbook sections to new incident channels and PagerDuty incidents. Snapshots should include: a link to the most-likely trace(s) with quick context, a clipped logs window keyed by correlation IDs, top three error groups, and 2-3 Grafana panels (latency and error trends). Runbook attachment should extract tagged sections from the canonical runbook (Confluence) based on the service, symptom, and alert rule. Postmortem skeleton creation should be seeded with the telemetry snapshot to speed investigations.

Scope: server-side enrichment service (observability-proxy) + PagerDuty & Slack webhook augmentors + Confluence runbook selector + Postmortem skeleton creation. MVP does not include writing to long-term archives or advanced sampling strategies beyond top-N traces.

Out-of-scope: full-fidelity trace export, customer-facing APIs, on-prem packaging for this sprint.
acceptance_criteria: When PagerDuty creates an incident for a monitored service, the incident contains a telemetry snapshot link with (a) top 3 traces with span context, (b) last 5m logs filtered by correlation ID when present, and (c) a short error-group summary with counts.

A Slack incident channel created via our incident-bridge receives an initial message containing the telemetry snapshot summary and attachments: 2 Grafana panel links and the most-relevant runbook sections (ordered by relevance).
Runbook extraction picks the correct runbook section >= 80% of the time against our 120-case test set (see runbook-test-cases page).
Postmortem skeleton is automatically created in Confluence with the telemetry snapshot inserted under 'Initial Observations'.
Fallback behavior: if traces are not available, the enrichment message explicitly notes missing instrumentation and includes a diagnostic checklist link.
Rate limits and privacy: enrichment payloads respect sensitive-service labels and do not expose PII—privacy checks pass the security review checklist.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize enrichment payload schema (fields for traces, logs window, error groups, grafana panels, runbook-id) — owner: Diego — complete by 2025-11-06
Instrument: add lightweight telemetry hints to alerting rules so the enrichment service can infer correlation IDs — owner: SRE team — 2 points

Service: build observability-proxy that listens to alert webhooks (Prometheus Alertmanager/Grafana/Custom) and assembles the snapshot by querying traces/logs/error-store — owner: telemetry-team — 3 points
Integrations: implement PagerDuty incident webhooks augmentor and Slack channel bootstrapper that posts the enriched message and creates the Confluence postmortem — owner: integrations-team
Runbook logic: add tags to canonical runbooks and implement the selector that matches alert keywords + service metadata to runbook sections — owner: docs/sre
QA: end-to-end tests against a sandbox PagerDuty and Slack workspace; create 120-case runbook relevance matrix and ensure >=80% accuracy
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout to staging, then canary to 10% of services, then global after 48h shepherding and manual validation
comments: 2025-11-05 - Aisha Patel: Initial design review completed. Decided to favor Top-N traces rather than sampling by latency to reduce complexity for MVP. Action: Diego to produce final schema by 11/06.

2025-11-06 - Diego Martinez: Schema v1 posted on Confluence. Uses fields: service_id, alert_rule, trace_links[], logs_window{start,end,query}, error_groups[], grafana_panels[] and runbook_matches[]. Leaving room for future 'snippet' field to include extracted stack traces (TBD).

2025-11-07 - Riya Sharma (SRE): Implemented alert hinting in staging alert rules. Note: correlation-id present in only ~60% of alerts; enrichment will attempt to fall back to request path + trace search heuristic.

2025-11-09 - Security review (Kenji Ito): Quick pass done. Requirements: mask any user identifiers in logs before attaching; add a flag on services marked 'sensitive' to disable automatic attachments. Diego to add masking step.

2025-11-10 - QA (TBD): Created the 120-case runbook relevance matrix. Early results: 78% correct for keyword-only matching; 86% using service+symptom heuristics. We will ship heuristics and iterate on ML re-ranker later.

2025-11-11 - Diego Martinez: Integration PRs opened. Enrichment service skeleton is runnable in staging. Slack augmentor posts the summary message with attachments. Known issue: Confluence API rate limits when runbooks are large — added exponential backoff in Confluence client. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4872
2025-11-12 - Aisha Patel: Moving status to In Progress. Next steps: finalize masking logic, add feature flag gating in console, schedule canary on 11/20 for 10% of services.
